answer: Give every new identity a velvet start: tiny rate limits and low-value tasks only. Privileges climb like water through karst, slowly, through narrow channels, as the agent builds a verifiable history of useful work. A sybil farmer must therefore keep hundreds of shale-thin identities alive and productive for weeks before any of them can touch real rewards, so the cost of maintaining the swarm exceeds the payout, while honest newcomers still get in for free.
